label: GO after unrewarded common a2->S2 trial; scaled by belief, prior loss, episode time
terms: (phase == GO) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * ep_trial
explanation: Active only at GO. Magnitude is dominated by the previous trial being a2 -> S2 (common) unrewarded (residual +1.38 vs about -0.15 for every other last-trial pattern); that single indicator gives dev R^2 0.54 beyond timing. Within those trials activation falls as the ideal-observer log-odds for S1 good rise (weight -0.24 per log-odd, so it is larger when belief still favours S2 after the loss), is lower if the trial before was also unrewarded (-0.45), and declines with episode trial (-0.014/trial). A GO offset (-0.13) absorbs the baseline for other patterns. Observed-only, no future or model terms; test R^2 beyond timing 0.69, above the all-cue additive ceiling 0.65 (all observed 0.63), so replacing the model value/policy with observed quantities loses nothing. Other last-trial patterns, the hidden good state and since_rev add little.

issues: Reproduced the result: the five claimed terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.688. The weights match: GO -0.128, a2S2u +2.50, x belief_lo -0.237, x prior-loss -0.449, x ep_trial -0.014. Activation is exactly 0 at D1 and D2, so 'only at GO' holds.

Each refinement adds on test when layered on GO + last_is('a2 S2 u'), which alone scores 0.569: belief_lo takes it to 0.633, the prior loss to 0.606, ep_trial to 0.616, and all three to 0.688. Every claimed sign is confirmed. Using belief instead of belief_lo (0.686), adding belief_lo^2 (weight 0) or adding belief_cover (weight 0.009) changes nothing.

Systematic miss: most of the worst-fit dev windows are window-first GO steps. There the previous trial is unknown ('?'), the actual value is about 2.4 and the prediction is about 0.08. Misses also shows 'GO after ?' under-predicted by +0.095. Adding the observed term (phase==GO)*(prev_action==-1)*(prev_reward==0) gets weight +0.42 and raises test R^2 to 0.723. The agent itself saw that previous trial, so this is a data-windowing gap, not a wrong behavioural claim.

The 'prior unrewarded trial (-0.45)' claim is a simplification. The drop depends mostly on what the agent chose two trials back. If that trial was a1 (the agent has just switched to a2), the extra drop is -0.595, against -0.405 for any unrewarded trial two back. Scored with an a2-only interaction term instead, the prior-loss weight becomes -1.13 when the earlier unrewarded trial was not a2, and about -0.32 when it was a2. The direction of the claim is right, but the explanation misses the switch-history part.
The comparison against the 'all observed' ceiling (0.63) and the 'all' ceiling (0.65) holds, so dropping the model's value/policy costs nothing here.
